text.tspan: flush · fsync · release — the same script
upload the buffer if it is dirty. Idempotent
a buffer for this inode?
in-memory map — no I/O to find out
Answer OK
nothing buffered: already flushed, or never written
an ignored file?
vim swap files, office lock files: they live entirely
in the buffer and never reach the server
Answer OK — keep the buffer
it IS the file's content until the file is removed
gone — unlinked meanwhile
(the editor deleted its own swap file)

g.text: FileIo drop the buffer, do not resurrect the file

text.tspan: the precondition — a decision, not a request
never uploaded before → If-None-Match: *
known ETag → If-Match: that one
otherwise → unconditional, never claiming the file is absent
Net chunked upload
bounded memory
FileIo read the buffer, then
Net conditional PUT
invalidate listings taken before this upload
so a stale PROPFIND cannot delete the file
we just materialised

g.text: DbWrite record the new ETag and size

text.tspan: FileIo copy the buffer into the blob cache
copied, never loaded whole — the cache stays hot
for the next read
Net PROPFIND the parent
so the row picks up its server-assigned file id.
Without it a later rename or delete would think the
file exists only locally
drop the buffer and the pending mtime
desktop indicator → Idle

g.text: Answer OK — the inode is idle again

text.tspan: keep the buffer and the pending mtime
desktop indicator → Error, and tell the user their
edit is still only local — data at risk is worth a
notification, and the next flush retries

g.text: Fail — the error to the caller

text.tspan: 412 — the precondition failed:
somebody else changed the file meanwhile.
The sub-script records the version, stores the bytes
and reconciles the parent itself, whichever way it
resolves — so all that is left here is to let the
buffer go. See the conflict diagram
The same callback carries the cancellation signal:
a flush while reads are still outstanding on this
handle means nobody is waiting for them any more.
Measured — the kernel delivers flush at once and
holds release back until every read is answered
